boundary_rationale: Onset: the book opens on two datelines in two counting systems - בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.1.1, a regnal/exilic year the book never names an era for) and הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין (oshb:Ezek.1.2, the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile) - followed at oshb:Ezek.1.3 by the superscription הָיֹ֣ה הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְ֠הוָה אֶל יְחֶזְקֵ֨אל, an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect word-event with a THIRD-PERSON addressee ('to Ezekiel', not 'to me'). This verb and addressee shape are why the verse sits in the 49-verse any-form word-event count and not the 48-verse first-person family (sweep: verses containing the word-event phrase in any form, 49; the 48 excludes this one verse by predicate). It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The same verse also carries וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָֽה, the hand-of-YHWH construct that opens the book's first vision (one of 7 verses carrying the construct). Close: the scene runs unbroken to oshb:Ezek.1.28, מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר, glossed by the WEB as “this was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh's glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke” (web:Ezek.1.28). No word-event, messenger, recognition or utterance formula interrupts 1:4-1:27 (the transport-verb and 'he said to me' sweeps that mark scene changes elsewhere in the book's visions do not begin until chapter 8), so the throne-theophany carries no formula-marked internal seam; the samekh recorded after 1:28 and the fresh 'he said to me' that opens oshb:Ezek.2.1 together mark the vision/commission seam on the FAR side of this unit; the onset evidence at oshb:Ezek.2.1 is weighed there.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating oshb:Ezek.1.1-1.3 as its own superscription unit, separate from the vision it introduces. Rejected because the vision proper (1:4-1:28) carries no independent onset device of its own - it simply continues the sentence the hand-of-YHWH clause opens - so cutting after 1:3 would manufacture a seam the bytes do not mark, and would still leave a 25-verse remainder with the same cap problem.
device_notes: Whole-chapter span (28 verses), well above the 7-10 typical density and above the 14-16 stretch cap for measured/listed blocks even though this is not such a block; disclosed and held at low confidence rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut. MT 1:3 is cited only under the 49-verse any-form word-event count (never blended with the 48-verse first-person family, per the denominator reconciliation). K/Q at 1:8 checked before quoting: the unit does not splice the disputed word. The OSHB editorial note at 1:11 is disclosed as single-witness apparatus, not a reading change. Paseq at 1:1 and 1:27 disclosed count-only (single-witness); no intra-verse position is claimed.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.1 וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן אָדָם֙ עֲמֹ֣ד עַל רַגְלֶ֔יךָ וַאֲדַבֵּ֖ר אֹתָֽךְ ('he said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet” (web:Ezek.2.1)') opens the commission immediately after the vision's samekh-marked close at oshb:Ezek.1.28. The sending proper follows at 2:3, שׁוֹלֵ֨חַ אֲנִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.2.3) ('I send you to the children of Israel'), continuing into the messenger formula כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.2.4), embedded as reported speech rather than a fresh onset. Pe marks fall after 2:2 and 2:5, disclosed as intra-row sub-paragraph texture, not unit cuts. Close: 2:7, the refrain-form כִּ֥י מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.2.7) ('for they are rebellious'), with a pe recorded after it, before a fresh sub-onset address opens at 2:8.

device_notes: Pe marks at 2:2 and 2:5 fall inside the unit and are disclosed as sub-paragraph texture (single-witness); neither coincides with a formula onset, so neither is read as a unit-cutting seam. The phrase בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י (oshb:Ezek.2.5) ('rebellious house') recurs at 2:5, inside the same address whose close at 2:7 echoes it. The samekh after oshb:Ezek.1.28 closes the preceding unit's own vision scene and is not this unit's onset evidence.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.8 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם … ('and you, son of man, hear…') opens a fresh sub-onset immediately after the refrain-marked pe close at oshb:Ezek.2.7. The scroll appears at 2:9, וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּה יָ֖ד שְׁלוּחָ֣ה אֵלָ֑י וְהִנֵּה (oshb:Ezek.2.9) ('behold, a hand stretched out to me'), and its inscription is read at 2:10, אֵלֶ֔יהָ קִנִ֥ים וָהֶ֖גֶה וָהִֽי (oshb:Ezek.2.10) ('lamentations, mourning, and woe'), with a samekh recorded after 2:10, disclosed as intra-row texture rather than a cut, since the eating that follows continues the same scroll scene: 3:1 reopens with a further 'he said to me,' אֱכוֹל֙ אֶת הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את (oshb:Ezek.3.1) ('eat this scroll'), intra-row, and the WEB chapter numeral falling at 2:10/3:1 is disclosed only as tier-4 texture, never as boundary evidence (E-23). Close: 3:3, וַתְּהִ֥י בְּפִ֖י כִּדְבַ֥שׁ לְמָתֽוֹק (oshb:Ezek.3.3) ('it was in my mouth as sweet as honey'), with a pe recorded after it, before the address turns from the scroll to the audience's character at 3:4.

The WEB paragraph/chapter break at 2:10/3:1 is named nowhere as boundary evidence (E-23).

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:4 לֶךְ בֹּא֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.3.4) ('go, get you to the house of Israel'), a fresh 'he said to me' turning from the scroll itself to the audience it will be spoken to; 3:7 characterizes them, כִּ֚י כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חִזְקֵי מֵ֥צַח וּקְשֵׁי לֵ֖ב הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.7) ('for all the house of Israel are obstinate and hard-hearted'). A pe is recorded after 3:9, כְּשָׁמִ֛יר חָזָ֥ק מִצֹּ֖ר נָתַ֣תִּי מִצְחֶ֑ךָ ('I have made your forehead as a diamond'), closing with a further rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּֽית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.9) (the third of six). That mark is disclosed but not read as the unit's own close: 3:10 reopens with 'moreover he said to me' on the same audience-description topic, and cutting there would leave 3:10-3:11 (2 verses, no word-event of its own) below the unit-size floor. Close: 3:11, אִֽם יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם יֶחְדָּֽלוּ (oshb:Ezek.3.11) ('whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse'), immediately before the return-transport of 3:12 begins a distinct, vision-texture scene.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 5:1 וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן אָדָ֜ם קַח לְךָ֣ חֶ֣רֶב חַדָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.5.1) ('you, son of man, take a sharp sword'), a fresh 'son of man' sub-onset distinct from 4:1's - a new symbolic object (sword/razor/hair) rather than a continuation of the siege-tile act. The messenger formula at 5:5, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.5.5), opens the act's own interpretation rather than a competing unit (no refrain close intervenes between the hair-sign and its meaning). The oath at 5:11, חַי אָ֗נִי ('as I live'), with the utterance signature נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.5.11) attached mid-verse, marks an emphatic sub-onset of the verdict paragraph, not a unit boundary. The formula 'I, Yahweh, have spoken' recurs three times, at 5:13 (אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ (oshb:Ezek.5.13)), 5:15 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.15)) and 5:17 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.17)); the first two are paragraph-final rather than unit-final because no fresh onset device follows either (5:14 continues 'moreover I will make you a desolation' with no messenger formula or word-event reopening the address). Close: 5:17, with a pe recorded after it, before 6:1 opens with a fresh strict word-event. The verdict continues in two further 'therefore' messenger formulae addressing the same party: 5:7, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.7) (2mp, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says'), and 5:8, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.8) (2fs, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says') — both verdict paragraphs inside the same interpretation, addressing Jerusalem and the people in her as one party, with no refrain standing before either (the samekh after 5:6, 5:7 and 5:9 are disclosed as intra-row texture, not unit-cutting seams). The verdict is bound to the sign-act itself by a byte-identical clause: 5:12 closes with the same words that close 5:2, וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.5.2; oshb:Ezek.5.12) ('and I will draw a sword after them', sweep: 3 verses book-wide, the third at 12:14).

The WEB's own paragraphing marks further breaks at 7:10, 7:15 and 7:23 (web:Ezek.7.23, opening 'make chains'); these are tier-4 and are disclosed as texture only, never as boundary evidence (E-23) — none coincides with a word-event, messenger formula or set-your-face reopening the address, so no internal cut is made.
